trajectory_summary: This call never had appointment-setting potential in the standard sense -- the customer is an existing solar owner with a 10kW system asking about battery backup, already contacted by Ion once before. The rep spent the call reactively discovering the shape of the request (existing system, prior quote, system-size constraint) rather than surfacing it early, and the call ended in a disqualification after a long, unexplained hold.
outcome_dispute: The v1 tag is unknown, but the observed outcome is a disqualification (dq) driven by a stated system-size-too-large-for-battery constraint discovered mid-call, not a booked or tentative appointment -- this should not be scored as a successful set.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: No utility bill was raised at any point; the conversation stayed on system size and a prior verbal quote for backup/battery, and the call ended in disqualification before bill collection would have been relevant.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Know the DQ criteria before the hold, not after it
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I was trying to get a specialist to come talk to you, but I was really fighting for you. But they they said your your kilowatt size is too big, and it's too big for a battery or a backup.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer stated his system size (10kW) at 01:16, four minutes before the rep discovered via a supervisor hold that it disqualified him for the backup program. A rep who knows the battery/backup size ceiling could have told the customer the outcome immediately instead of running him through a near-minute hold for a question the rep already had the data to answer.
